messages:
maria (eng-security): heads-up: we just saw a KMS decrypt latency spike in us-west-2 that caused app-level 5xxs for a few minutes. :warning:
jonah (infra): saw the same, alerted by svc-decrypt error rate. stack traces show `kms.Decrypt` timing out at ~3s repeatedly.
kms-bot: ALERT: aws-kms us-west-2 API 5xx rate increase detected (2026-03-19T21:07:12Z).
ashley (eng-sre): did any recent RBAC or policy changes touch the kms role?
maria (eng-security): no policy pushes this week. my hypothesis: a scheduled background key-rotation job kicked off and generated a high fanout of `Decrypt` calls. that bumped us into KMS throttling / elevated latency.
kevin (platform): interesting — rotation starts daily at 21:00 UTC by default. rotation job recently expanded to include some previously-excluded namespaces (PR #4823).
jonah (infra): logs: many concurrent `Decrypt` requests from rotation-runner@infra with identical ciphertext sizes. KMS returned 429/500 intermittently then latency climbed. snippet: {"requestId":"...","status":429,"operation":"Decrypt","latency_ms":3120}
ashley (eng-sre): we did see the client code retry aggressively (exponential backoff but small base) which may have amplified load. runbook fallback kicked in for session-token flows (we have a DEK cache there). others hit KMS directly and failed.
maria (eng-security): immediate mitigations applied: paused rotation job (kevin), increased local DEK cache TTL to 12h for user-session flows (ashley), and bumped circuit-breaker threshold for decrypt to fail-fast.
kevin (platform): applied quota increase request to AWS console and opened support ticket. added 200ms randomized jitter to rotation job to smooth fanout.
jonah (infra): followup: we need to ensure envelope-decryption fallback is enabled universally. current state: some services check local DEK cache first, others don't. that's a gap.
maria (eng-security): agreed. action items: 1) audit services for DEK cache usage + ensure consistent client library that does `try-local-cache -> async-prefetch -> kms-decrypt` flow, 2) add a canary for rotation job that simulates small decrypt load before full rollout, 3) update runbook with KMS throttling playbook (what to pause, what to cache).
oncall-sre: added to incidents channel and created ticket SEC-4271 for postmortem and followups.
jonah (infra): proposed code snippet for client-side fallback (please copy into common SDK): // decrypt wrapper
if (localDekCache.exists(ciphertextId)) return localDekCache.get(ciphertextId);
// prefetch async, but return cached or error quickly
const dek = await kms.decrypt({CiphertextBlob: ciphertext});
localDekCache.set(ciphertextId, dek, TTL_MS);
return dek;
maria (eng-security): also we noticed audit-logs for decrypt were noisy during the spike. we should add sampling to audit logs at very high KMS volumes so backend logging doesn't saturate.
ashley (eng-sre): runbook updates: add `pause-rotation` play, `increase-local-cache-ttl`, `rollback-rotation-pr`, `open-aws-support` steps. I'll draft and push.
kevin (platform): long-term: consider an envelope encryption broker that handles rotation centrally and exposes cached DEKs over an internal authenticated endpoint (with RBAC and auditing) so services aren't hitting KMS directly.
maria (eng-security): agree — design doc required. also: re-evaluate key rotation schedules to avoid peak windows by default and put rotations behind controlled canaries.
oncall-sre: postmortem checklist created, scheduled 1hr async doc review. tagging @kevin @jonah @ashley. :thumbsup:
jonah (infra): closing note: no data was exposed, decrypt failures were transient. classified as near-miss. we'll follow the action items and update SEC-4271.
kevin (platform): thanks team. I'll keep the support ticket open until AWS confirms no service degradation on their side. :rotating_light:
